chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Jameela, from Sa'd al-Iskaf, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) passed by food in the market of Medina, so he said to its owner: 'I do not see your food except as good,' and he asked him about its price. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to him that he should insert his hands into the food, so he did, and he brought out food that had perished. So he said to its owner: 'I do not see you except as having gathered betrayal and cheating for the Muslims.'

key_terms.يَدُسَّ: to insert or push in deeply

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on hiding defective goods in trade?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the concept of *ghish* (deception) in trade, where the Prophet (peace be upon him) was divinely guided to uncover hidden flaws in a merchant's goods, demonstrating that commercial integrity is a matter of both legal and spiritual accountability. In Shia jurisprudence, this incident serves as a primary evidence for the prohibition of *ghish* in sales, emphasizing that concealing defects invalidates the fairness of the transaction. The narrative underscores the Prophet's role as a divinely inspired inspector of market ethics, linking commercial honesty directly to communal trust.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Jameela, from Sa’ad Al Askaaf, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The Prophet<sup>saww</sup> passed in a food market stall of Al-Medina, so he<sup>saww</sup> said to its owner: ‘I<sup>saww</sup> do not see your food except as good’, and he<sup>saww</sup> asked him about its price. So Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Revealed unto him<sup>saww</sup> that he<sup>saww</sup> should insert his<sup>saww</sup> hand in the food. So he<sup>saww</sup> did it, and there came out food which had perished. So he<sup>saww</sup> said to its owner: ‘I<sup>saww</sup> do not see you except as having gathered betrayal and cheating for the Muslims’.
en.sarwar: 7. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from ibn Mahbub from abu Jamilah from Sa‘d al-Iskaf who has said the following: “Abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

Once, in the market place of al-Madinah, the Holy Prophet, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, passed by a place where food was sold. The Holy Prophet said, to the owner, “I can see your food is good.” He then asked about its price. Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, sent revelation and told him to check the lower levels of the food for sale. When he checked a bad quality of food came out. He then said to the owner, “Now I can see you have collected betrayal and cheating for the Muslims.’””
